tools.name: github_search_repositories
tools.description: Search GitHub repositories using GitHub search syntax (e.g. 'language:go stars:>1000 topic:cli'). Use this to discover repositories when you do not know the exact owner/name; use github_get_repository when you already know it. Results are paginated, max 100 per page, and rate limited to 30 requests per minute.

query.description: Search query using GitHub repository search qualifiers.

sort.description: Field to sort results by; defaults to best match.

tools.name: github_get_repository
tools.description: Get metadata for a single repository including description, default branch, visibility, topics, license, and star/fork counts. Use this when you know the owner and name; use github_search_repositories to discover repos. Works for any repo the token can read.

owner.description: Account name of the repository owner.

repo.description: Name of the repository without the owner.

tools.name: github_create_repository
tools.description: Create a new repository for the authenticated user or in an organization. Requires the 'repo' scope (or 'public_repo' for public ones). Fails if the name is already taken in that account.

org.description: Organization to create the repo in; omit for personal account.

private.description: Whether the repository should be private.

auto_init.description: Create an initial commit with an empty README.

tools.name: github_fork_repository
tools.description: Fork a repository to the authenticated user's account or a specified organization. Forking is asynchronous, so the new fork may take a few seconds to be available.

owner.description: Owner of the repository to fork.

repo.description: Name of the repository to fork.

organization.description: Organization to fork into; defaults to the user account.

name.description: Optional new name for the fork.

tools.name: github_get_file_contents
tools.description: Read a file or list a directory from a repository at a given ref. Returns decoded text for files and entries for directories. Use github_search_code to find files by content instead of path.

path.description: Path of the file or directory in the repository.

ref.description: Branch, tag, or commit SHA; defaults to the default branch.

tools.name: github_create_or_update_file
tools.description: Create a new file or update an existing one in a single commit. When updating, you must pass the current blob SHA of the file. Use github_push_files to commit several files at once.

path.description: Path of the file to create or update.

content.description: New file content as plain text.

sha.description: Blob SHA of the file being replaced; required for updates.

tools.name: github_push_files
tools.description: Commit multiple files to a branch in a single commit. Prefer this over github_create_or_update_file when changing more than one file. The branch must already exist.

files.description: Files to include in the commit.

tools.name: github_search_code
tools.description: Search file contents across GitHub using code search syntax (e.g. 'addClass repo:jquery/jquery language:js'). Use this to find where a symbol or string appears; use github_get_file_contents when you know the path. Limited to files under 384KB and rate limited.

query.description: Code search query with qualifiers like repo:, path:, language:.

sort.description: Sort field; omit for best match.

tools.name: github_list_branches
tools.description: List branches in a repository, optionally only protected ones. Paginated. Use github_list_commits to see history on a branch.

protected.description: Only return protected branches when true.

tools.name: github_create_branch
tools.description: Create a new branch from a given commit SHA or from an existing branch. Fails if the branch name already exists.

from_branch.description: Source branch; defaults to the repo default branch.

sha.description: Commit SHA to branch from; overrides from_branch.

tools.name: github_list_commits
tools.description: List commits on a branch or for a path, newest first. Supports filtering by author and date range. Use github_get_commit for the diff of a single commit.

sha.description: Branch name or commit SHA to start listing from.

author.description: GitHub username or email of the commit author.

since.description: ISO 8601 timestamp; only commits after this date.

until.description: ISO 8601 timestamp; only commits before this date.

tools.name: github_get_commit
tools.description: Get details of a single commit including message, author, stats, and changed files with patches. Use github_list_commits to find the SHA first.

sha.description: Commit SHA, branch, or tag name.

include_diff.description: Include file patches in the response.

tools.name: github_list_issues
tools.description: List issues in a repository filtered by state, labels, assignee, or update time. Pull requests are excluded. Use github_search_issues for cross-repo or free-text queries.

labels.description: Only issues having all of these labels.

assignee.description: Username of assignee, or '*' for any.

since.description: ISO 8601 timestamp; only issues updated after this.

tools.name: github_search_issues
tools.description: Search issues and pull requests across GitHub using search syntax (e.g. 'is:issue is:open label:bug repo:org/name author:alice'). Use this for free-text or cross-repository queries; use github_list_issues for simple per-repo listing.

query.description: Search query with qualifiers such as is:, label:, repo:, author:.

tools.name: github_get_issue
tools.description: Get a single issue by number with its body, labels, assignees, milestone, and state. Use github_list_issue_comments for the discussion thread.

tools.name: github_create_issue
tools.description: Create a new issue in a repository. Requires write or triage access for labels, assignees, and milestone to be applied; otherwise those fields are ignored. Use github_update_issue to modify an existing one.

tools.name: github_update_issue
tools.description: Update an existing issue's title, body, state, labels, assignees, or milestone. Passing labels or assignees replaces the existing set. Use this to close or reopen an issue; use github_add_issue_comment to just reply.

issue_number.description: Number of the issue to update.

tools.name: github_add_issue_comment
tools.description: Add a comment to an issue or pull request conversation. For inline code review comments on a diff, use github_create_pull_request_review instead.

tools.name: github_list_issue_comments
tools.description: List comments on an issue or pull request conversation in chronological order. Paginated. Does not include inline review comments.

since.description: ISO 8601 timestamp; only comments updated after this.

tools.name: github_list_pull_requests
tools.description: List pull requests in a repository filtered by state, base or head branch. Use github_search_issues with is:pr for text or cross-repo searches. Paginated.

head.description: Filter by head in the form 'user:branch'.

tools.name: github_get_pull_request
tools.description: Get a pull request's details: title, body, state, mergeability, head and base refs, and change counts. Use github_get_pull_request_diff for the actual patch or github_list_pull_request_files for the file list.

tools.name: github_get_pull_request_diff
tools.description: Fetch the unified diff of a pull request as text. Large diffs may be truncated; use github_list_pull_request_files for a per-file breakdown.

max_bytes.description: Maximum diff size to return in bytes.

tools.name: github_list_pull_request_files
tools.description: List files changed in a pull request with status, additions, deletions, and patch per file. Paginated up to 3000 files.

tools.name: github_create_pull_request
tools.description: Open a new pull request from a head branch into a base branch. The head branch must already be pushed. Supports draft PRs and maintainer edits.

owner.description: Repository owner of the base repo.

head.description: Branch containing changes, or 'user:branch' for forks.

draft.description: Create as a draft pull request.

maintainer_can_modify.description: Allow maintainers to push to the head branch.

tools.name: github_merge_pull_request
tools.description: Merge an open pull request using merge, squash, or rebase. Fails if the PR is not mergeable or required checks and reviews are missing. Requires write access.

commit_message.description: Extra detail for the merge commit message.

tools.name: github_create_pull_request_review
tools.description: Submit a review on a pull request: approve, request changes, or comment, optionally with inline comments on specific lines. Use github_add_issue_comment for a plain conversation comment.

tools.name: github_list_workflow_runs
tools.description: List GitHub Actions workflow runs for a repository, filterable by workflow, branch, status, and actor. Use this to check CI status; use github_get_workflow_run for one run's details.

workflow_id.description: Workflow file name or numeric id.

status.description: Filter by run status or conclusion.

actor.description: Only runs triggered by this user.

tools.name: github_get_workflow_run
tools.description: Get details of one workflow run including conclusion, timing, triggering commit, and attempt number. Use github_list_workflow_runs to find the run id.

exclude_pull_requests.description: Omit associated pull requests from the response.

tools.name: github_rerun_workflow
tools.description: Re-run a workflow run, optionally only the failed jobs. Requires write access to Actions. Returns immediately; poll the run for results.

run_id.description: Id of the workflow run to re-run.

failed_only.description: Re-run only failed jobs and their dependents.

tools.name: github_list_releases
tools.description: List releases of a repository, newest first, including drafts if the token has push access. Paginated.

tasks.prompt: Find popular Rust command-line tools on GitHub with more than 5000 stars, sorted by stars.
Show me all open issues in kubernetes/kubernetes labeled 'kind/bug' that are assigned to anyone, newest updated first.
Search across all of GitHub for open issues mentioning 'memory leak' in the facebook org that were created by user alice.
Close issue #482 in acme/billing-api as not planned.
Squash-merge PR 77 in acme/web-frontend with the title 'Add dark mode'.
Rerun only the failed jobs from CI run 9981234 in acme/web-frontend.

tools.name: slack_list_channels
tools.description: List channels in the workspace, including public channels and optionally private channels, DMs, and group DMs the bot or user can see. Use this to browse or enumerate channels; use slack_search_channels when you only know part of a channel name. Results are paginated; pass the returned next_cursor to fetch more.

types.description: Comma-separated channel types to include: public_channel, private_channel, mpim, im.

limit.description: Maximum number of channels to return per page (1-1000).

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response.

team_id.description: Workspace ID, required only for org-level tokens.

tools.name: slack_search_channels
tools.description: Find channels whose name, topic, or purpose matches a text query. Prefer this over slack_list_channels when you have a keyword but not the channel ID. Returns up to the requested number of matches ranked by relevance.

query.description: Text to match against channel name, topic, or purpose.

include_private.description: Whether to include private channels the caller is a member of.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return.

tools.name: slack_get_channel_info
tools.description: Get metadata for a single channel, including its topic, purpose, creation date, and member count. Use slack_list_channels for many channels at once. Requires the channel ID, not the name.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel, e.g. C0123456789.

include_num_members.description: Whether to include the member count.

include_locale.description: Whether to include the channel locale.

tools.name: slack_create_channel
tools.description: Create a new public or private channel. Channel names must be lowercase, without spaces or periods, and at most 80 characters. Fails if the name is already taken.

name.description: Name of the new channel, lowercase with hyphens or underscores.

is_private.description: Create a private channel instead of a public one.

team_id.description: Workspace ID, required for org-level tokens.

description.description: Optional purpose to set after creation.

tools.name: slack_archive_channel
tools.description: Archive a channel so it becomes read-only and hidden from default lists. Use this instead of deleting; archived channels can be restored by an admin. Requires channel-management permissions.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel to archive.

tools.name: slack_rename_channel
tools.description: Rename an existing channel. The new name must follow Slack naming rules (lowercase, no spaces, max 80 characters). Use slack_set_channel_topic to change the topic instead.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel to rename.

tools.name: slack_set_channel_topic
tools.description: Set or replace the topic of a channel. Use slack_set_channel_purpose for the longer description of what the channel is for. Topics are limited to 250 characters.

topic.description: New topic text, up to 250 characters.

tools.name: slack_set_channel_purpose
tools.description: Set the purpose (description) of a channel. Use slack_set_channel_topic for the short headline shown in the channel header. Limited to 250 characters.

tools.name: slack_invite_to_channel
tools.description: Invite one or more users to a channel. Use slack_get_user_by_email or slack_search_users first if you only have an email or name. Up to 100 user IDs per call.

user_ids.description: List of user IDs to invite (max 100).

force.description: Continue inviting valid users even if some IDs are invalid.

tools.name: slack_remove_from_channel
tools.description: Remove a user from a channel. Requires permission to manage channel membership. Cannot remove users from #general.

user_id.description: ID of the user to remove.

tools.name: slack_list_channel_members
tools.description: List the user IDs of members of a channel. Returns IDs only; use slack_get_user_profile to resolve details. Paginated via cursor.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response.

tools.name: slack_post_message
tools.description: Post a new message to a channel or DM, optionally as a reply in a thread. Use slack_reply_to_thread when replying to an existing thread is the primary intent, and slack_schedule_message to send later. Supports mrkdwn text and Block Kit blocks.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel or DM to post in.

text.description: Message text in mrkdwn; used as fallback when blocks are provided.

blocks.description: Optional Block Kit blocks for rich layout.

thread_ts.description: Timestamp of a parent message to post into its thread.

unfurl_links.description: Whether to unfurl links in the message.

reply_broadcast.description: When replying in a thread, also show it in the channel.

tools.name: slack_reply_to_thread
tools.description: Reply to an existing message thread. Needs the channel ID and the parent message timestamp. Use slack_post_message for top-level messages.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel containing the thread.

broadcast.description: Also send the reply to the channel.

tools.name: slack_update_message
tools.description: Edit the text or blocks of a message previously posted by this bot or user. Cannot edit other people's messages. Requires the channel ID and original message timestamp.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel containing the message.

ts.description: Timestamp of the message to edit.

tools.name: slack_delete_message
tools.description: Delete a message by channel ID and timestamp. Only messages authored by the caller can be deleted unless the token has admin rights. This cannot be undone.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel containing the message.

ts.description: Timestamp of the message to delete.

tools.name: slack_schedule_message
tools.description: Schedule a message to be posted at a future time, up to 120 days ahead. Use slack_post_message for immediate delivery. Returns a scheduled_message_id.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel or DM.

post_at.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the message should be sent.

thread_ts.description: Optional parent timestamp to post in a thread.

tools.name: slack_get_channel_history
tools.description: Fetch recent messages from a channel in reverse chronological order, optionally bounded by a time range. Use slack_get_thread_replies for replies in a thread and slack_search_messages to find messages by content. Paginated via cursor.

oldest.description: Only messages after this Unix timestamp.

latest.description: Only messages before this Unix timestamp.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response.

tools.name: slack_get_thread_replies
tools.description: Get all replies in a message thread, including the parent message. Use slack_get_channel_history for top-level messages. Requires the parent message timestamp.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel containing the thread.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response.

tools.name: slack_search_messages
tools.description: Search messages across the workspace using Slack search syntax (e.g. in:#general from:@alice after:2024-01-01 has:link). Use slack_get_channel_history when you just need recent messages from a known channel. Requires a user token with search:read.

query.description: Search query with optional modifiers like in:, from:, before:, after:.

tools.name: slack_get_permalink
tools.description: Get a permanent URL for a specific message. Use this when the user wants a shareable link to a message.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel containing the message.

tools.name: slack_add_reaction
tools.description: Add an emoji reaction to a message. Provide the emoji name without colons. Fails if the same reaction was already added by the caller.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel containing the message.

timestamp.description: Timestamp of the message to react to.

name.description: Emoji name without colons, e.g. thumbsup.

tools.name: slack_remove_reaction
tools.description: Remove an emoji reaction previously added by the caller from a message. Use slack_get_reactions to see which reactions exist.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel containing the message.

tools.name: slack_get_reactions
tools.description: List all reactions on a single message with the users who added each one. Use this to check approvals or votes expressed as emoji.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel containing the message.

full.description: Return the full list of users for each reaction instead of a truncated list.

tools.name: slack_list_users
tools.description: List all users in the workspace with basic profile fields. Use slack_search_users to find someone by name and slack_get_user_by_email for an exact email lookup. Paginated via cursor; may be slow in large workspaces.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response.

team_id.description: Workspace ID, required for org-level tokens.

tools.name: slack_search_users
tools.description: Search users by display name, real name, or handle. Use this when you have a partial name and need the user ID. Returns the best matches with ID, name, and title.

query.description: Name or handle fragment to search for.

tools.name: slack_get_user_by_email
tools.description: Look up a single user by exact email address. Use this over slack_search_users when you have a full email. Returns an error if no match exists.

tools.name: slack_get_user_profile
tools.description: Get the full profile of a user by ID, including title, timezone, status, and custom fields. Use slack_list_users for a basic overview of many users.

user_id.description: ID of the user, e.g. U0123456789.

include_labels.description: Include labels for custom profile fields.

tools.name: slack_upload_file
tools.description: Upload a file or text snippet to one or more channels. Provide either text content or base64-encoded bytes. Optionally attach an initial comment and thread.

channel_ids.description: Channels to share the file in.

filename.description: Name of the file including extension.

content.description: Text content or base64-encoded bytes of the file.

initial_comment.description: Message to post with the file.

thread_ts.description: Parent message timestamp to upload into a thread.

tools.name: slack_open_conversation
tools.description: Open or resume a direct message or group DM with one or more users and return its channel ID. Use this before posting a DM when you only have user IDs.

user_ids.description: One user ID for a DM, or 2-8 for a group DM.

return_im.description: Return the full conversation object instead of only its ID.

tools.name: sentry_list_organizations
tools.description: List all Sentry organizations the authenticated token has access to. Use this first to discover organization slugs required by most other tools. Results are paginated via cursor.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response.

owner.description: Only return organizations where the user is an owner.

query.description: Filter organizations by name or slug substring.

tools.name: sentry_list_projects
tools.description: List projects in an organization. Use to discover project slugs before querying issues or events. For details on a single project use sentry_get_project.

query.description: Filter projects by name or slug.

tools.name: sentry_get_project
tools.description: Retrieve full details for one project, including platform, teams, features, and options. Use sentry_list_projects when you only need to browse names.

tools.name: sentry_create_project
tools.description: Create a new project under a team. Requires project:write permission. Returns the project and optionally a DSN via sentry_list_client_keys.

team_slug.description: Team that will own the project.

slug.description: Optional URL slug; derived from name if omitted.

platform.description: Platform identifier such as python, javascript-react, or node.

tools.name: sentry_update_project
tools.description: Update project settings such as name, slug, platform, or resolve-age. Requires project:write. Use sentry_create_project for new projects.

resolve_age.description: Hours of inactivity after which issues auto-resolve.

tools.name: sentry_list_teams
tools.description: List teams in an organization with member counts and project access. Use to find team slugs for project creation or assignment.

query.description: Filter teams by name or slug.

tools.name: sentry_list_issues
tools.description: List issues for an organization or project using simple filters like status and time period. Use sentry_search_issues for free-form Sentry query syntax. Paginated via cursor.

tools.name: sentry_search_issues
tools.description: Search issues using Sentry's query syntax (e.g. 'is:unresolved level:error assigned:me browser.name:Chrome'). Prefer this over sentry_list_issues when filtering by tags, assignee, release, or text. Supports multiple projects and environments.

query.description: Sentry search query string.

tools.name: sentry_get_issue
tools.description: Fetch summary metadata for an issue: title, status, assignee, counts, first/last seen. Use sentry_get_issue_details for stack traces and the latest event.

issue_id.description: Issue ID or short ID like PROJ-123.

tools.name: sentry_get_issue_details
tools.description: Get in-depth information about an issue including the latest event's stack trace, breadcrumbs, tags, and contexts. Heavier than sentry_get_issue; use it when debugging the root cause.

issue_id.description: Issue ID or short ID like PROJ-123.

tools.name: sentry_update_issue
tools.description: Update a single issue's status, assignee, priority, or bookmark state. Use sentry_bulk_update_issues for many issues at once.

assigned_to.description: User email, user:ID, or team:slug; empty string to unassign.

is_bookmarked.description: Bookmark the issue for the current user.

tools.name: sentry_bulk_update_issues
tools.description: Apply the same update to many issues, selected by IDs or by a query. Use for mass resolve, ignore, or merge operations. Requires event:write.

query.description: Alternative to issue_ids: update all issues matching this query.

merge.description: Merge the selected issues into one.

tools.name: sentry_delete_issue
tools.description: Permanently delete an issue and its events. This cannot be undone; prefer resolving or ignoring. Requires event:admin.

tools.name: sentry_list_issue_events
tools.description: List events (individual occurrences) belonging to an issue, newest first. Use to compare occurrences or find one by tag. Paginated.

query.description: Filter events by tag query.

tools.name: sentry_get_event
tools.description: Retrieve one event by ID within a project, including its full payload, stack trace, and tags.

tools.name: sentry_search_events
tools.description: Query aggregated event data (Discover) with fields, filters, and sorting, e.g. count of errors by URL or p95 transaction duration. Use for analytics rather than individual issues.

query.description: Discover query filter.

sort.description: Field to sort by; prefix with - for descending.

tools.name: sentry_list_releases
tools.description: List releases for an organization or project, newest first, with commit and deploy summaries. Use sentry_get_release for a single release.

query.description: Filter by version prefix.

tools.name: sentry_get_release
tools.description: Get details of a specific release: commits, authors, new issue count, deploys, and adoption.

tools.name: sentry_create_release
tools.description: Create a new release and optionally associate commits and projects. Use at deploy time to enable suspect commits and regression tracking.

version.description: Release version, e.g. a git SHA or semver.

projects.description: Project slugs the release belongs to.

tools.name: sentry_create_deploy
tools.description: Record a deploy of a release to an environment. Use after sentry_create_release to mark when a version went live.

tools.name: sentry_list_alert_rules
tools.description: List issue alert rules for a project, including conditions, actions, and frequency. For metric alerts use sentry_list_metric_alerts.

tools.name: sentry_create_alert_rule
tools.description: Create an issue alert rule with conditions, filters, and actions such as Slack or email notifications. Requires alerts:write.

tools.name: sentry_list_metric_alerts
tools.description: List metric alert rules (thresholds on error counts, latency, crash-free rate) for an organization. For issue-based rules use sentry_list_alert_rules.

tools.name: sentry_list_client_keys
tools.description: List client keys (DSNs) for a project. Use to find the DSN to configure an SDK.

tools.name: sentry_create_client_key
tools.description: Create a new DSN client key for a project, optionally with a rate limit. Requires project:write.

tools.name: sentry_list_members
tools.description: List members of an organization with roles and teams. Use to resolve emails before assigning issues.

query.description: Filter by name or email.

tools.name: sentry_analyze_issue_with_seer
tools.description: Run Seer AI root-cause analysis on an issue and return suspected cause and proposed fix. May take up to a minute on first call; later calls return cached results.

tools.name: sentry_get_trace
tools.description: Fetch a distributed trace by trace ID, returning spans, durations, and associated errors. Use to investigate slow requests across services.

tools.name: sentry_list_issue_tag_values
tools.description: List the top values of a tag (e.g. browser, release, user) for an issue with counts. Use to see what is common across occurrences.

tag_key.description: Tag key such as browser, os, environment, release.

tools.name: sentry_list_replays
tools.description: List session replays with filtering by project, user, or error count. Use to find user sessions tied to an issue.

query.description: Replay search query, e.g. 'count_errors:>0'.

tools.name: grafana_search_dashboards
tools.description: Search dashboards and folders by title, tag, or folder using Grafana's search API. Use this to discover dashboards when you do not know the UID; use grafana_get_dashboard once you have a UID. Results are paginated with limit and page. Requires dashboards:read permission.

query.description: Text to match against dashboard titles.

tags.description: Only return dashboards having all of these tags.

folder_uids.description: Restrict results to these folder UIDs.

starred.description: Only return dashboards starred by the current user.

limit.description: Maximum number of results per page.

tools.name: grafana_get_dashboard
tools.description: Fetch the full JSON model of a dashboard by UID, including panels, templating variables, and metadata. Output can be large; use grafana_get_dashboard_summary for a compact overview. Requires dashboards:read permission.

include_meta.description: Include metadata such as folder, version, and permissions.

version.description: Specific version to fetch; defaults to latest.

tools.name: grafana_get_dashboard_summary
tools.description: Return a compact summary of a dashboard: title, tags, panel titles and types, variables, and refresh interval. Prefer this over grafana_get_dashboard when you only need to understand what a dashboard shows and want to save context.

tools.name: grafana_create_dashboard
tools.description: Create a new dashboard from a JSON model in a given folder. Fails if a dashboard with the same title exists in that folder unless overwrite is true. To modify an existing dashboard use grafana_update_dashboard. Requires dashboards:create permission.

folder_uid.description: UID of the destination folder; omit for General.

type.description: Panel type, e.g. timeseries, stat, table.

datasource_uid.description: UID of the panel data source.

panels.description: Panels to include in the dashboard.

overwrite.description: Overwrite an existing dashboard with the same title.

tools.name: grafana_update_dashboard
tools.description: Update an existing dashboard by UID, either by replacing its full JSON model or by applying targeted changes such as title, tags, or panel edits. Provide the current version to avoid overwriting concurrent edits. Requires dashboards:write permission.

uid.description: UID of the dashboard to update.

version.description: Expected current version for optimistic concurrency.

tools.name: grafana_delete_dashboard
tools.description: Permanently delete a dashboard by UID. This cannot be undone through the API, so confirm with the user first. Requires dashboards:delete permission.

uid.description: UID of the dashboard to delete.

force.description: Delete even if the dashboard is provisioned (may be recreated).

reason.description: Optional note recorded for audit purposes.

tools.name: grafana_get_dashboard_versions
tools.description: List the version history of a dashboard, including version number, author, timestamp, and commit message. Use before restoring or comparing versions. Supports pagination.

start.description: Offset to start from for pagination.

tools.name: grafana_restore_dashboard_version
tools.description: Restore a dashboard to a previous version, creating a new version with the old content. Find version numbers with grafana_get_dashboard_versions. Requires dashboards:write permission.

tools.name: grafana_list_folders
tools.description: List folders, optionally nested under a parent folder. Use to find folder UIDs for creating dashboards or setting permissions. Paginated.

parent_uid.description: List only subfolders of this folder UID.

tools.name: grafana_create_folder
tools.description: Create a new folder, optionally nested under a parent folder, to organize dashboards and alert rules. Requires folders:create permission.

uid.description: Optional custom UID; generated if omitted.

parent_uid.description: UID of the parent folder for nesting.

tools.name: grafana_list_datasources
tools.description: List all configured data sources with their UID, name, type, and default flag. Use this first to find the datasource UID needed by query tools. Does not return secrets. Requires datasources:read permission.

type.description: Filter by plugin type, e.g. prometheus, loki, tempo, postgres.

name_contains.description: Filter by substring of the data source name.

tools.name: grafana_get_datasource
tools.description: Get the full configuration of one data source by UID or name, including URL, access mode, and JSON options. Secure fields are redacted. Use grafana_list_datasources to browse.

name.description: Name of the data source; used if uid is not given.

tools.name: grafana_query_prometheus
tools.description: Execute a PromQL query against a Prometheus-compatible data source, as an instant or range query. Use for metrics investigation; for logs use grafana_query_loki. Large ranges are downsampled by step.

datasource_uid.description: UID of the Prometheus data source.

start.description: Start time, RFC3339 or relative like now-1h.

end.description: End time, RFC3339 or relative like now.

tools.name: grafana_list_prometheus_metric_names
tools.description: List metric names available in a Prometheus data source, optionally filtered by regex. Use to discover what can be queried before writing PromQL. Paginated by limit.

datasource_uid.description: UID of the Prometheus data source.

tools.name: grafana_list_prometheus_label_values
tools.description: List values for a label in a Prometheus data source, such as job or instance, optionally restricted by series matchers. Useful to build precise selectors.

datasource_uid.description: UID of the Prometheus data source.

matchers.description: Series selectors that restrict the results.

tools.name: grafana_query_loki
tools.description: Run a LogQL query against a Loki data source and return log lines or metric samples. Use for log investigation. Use grafana_get_loki_stats to check volume first on broad selectors.

datasource_uid.description: UID of the Loki data source.

start.description: Start time, RFC3339 or relative like now-1h.

tools.name: grafana_get_loki_stats
tools.description: Return stream, chunk, entry, and byte counts for a Loki selector over a time range. Use to estimate query cost before running grafana_query_loki.

datasource_uid.description: UID of the Loki data source.

tools.name: grafana_list_alert_rules
tools.description: List Grafana-managed alert rules with their current state and labels. Use to browse or filter rules; use grafana_get_alert_rule for full definition of one rule. Paginated.

tools.name: grafana_get_alert_rule
tools.description: Get the full definition of an alert rule by UID, including queries, conditions, evaluation interval, annotations, and notification settings.

tools.name: grafana_create_alert_rule
tools.description: Create a Grafana-managed alert rule with queries, a condition, and labels. Rules must live in a folder and rule group. To change an existing rule use grafana_update_alert_rule. Requires alert.rules:create permission.

folder_uid.description: Folder that will contain the rule.

rule_group.description: Rule group name; created if absent.

ref_id.description: Query reference ID such as A.

queries.description: Queries and expressions evaluated by the rule.

condition.description: RefID of the query or expression that triggers the alert.

for.description: Duration the condition must hold before firing, e.g. 5m.

labels.description: Labels attached to alerts, used for routing.

tools.name: grafana_update_alert_rule
tools.description: Update fields of an existing alert rule by UID, such as title, condition, pending period, labels, or paused state. Unspecified fields are kept. Requires alert.rules:write permission.

tools.name: grafana_list_contact_points
tools.description: List notification contact points (Slack, email, PagerDuty, webhook, etc.) with names and types. Sensitive settings are redacted. Use to find names for notification policies.

name.description: Filter by exact contact point name.

type.description: Filter by integration type such as slack or email.

tools.name: grafana_get_notification_policy
tools.description: Get the notification policy routing tree, showing matchers, contact points, grouping, and timing for each route. Use to determine where an alert with given labels would be sent.

flatten.description: Return routes as a flat list instead of a nested tree.

contact_point.description: Only show routes using this contact point.

label_matchers.description: Show routes matching these label matchers.

tools.name: grafana_create_annotation
tools.description: Create an annotation on a dashboard panel or organization-wide, such as marking a deployment or incident. Supports point-in-time and region annotations.

time_end.description: End time in epoch ms for region annotations.

dashboard_uid.description: Dashboard to attach to; omit for org-wide.

tools.name: grafana_list_annotations
tools.description: Query annotations by time range, tags, dashboard, or type. Useful for correlating deployments or incidents with metrics. Limited by limit parameter.

from.description: Start of range in epoch ms.

to.description: End of range in epoch ms.

tools.name: grafana_list_teams
tools.description: Search teams in the organization by name, returning ID, name, email, and member count. Paginated. Requires teams:read permission.

query.description: Team name substring.

tools.name: grafana_list_users
tools.description: Search users in the current organization by login, email, or name. Returns ID, login, role, and last-seen. Requires org.users:read permission.

query.description: Search text for login, email, or name.

tools.name: grafana_create_service_account
tools.description: Create a service account with a role for programmatic API access. Create tokens for it separately. Requires serviceaccounts:create permission.

is_disabled.description: Create the account in a disabled state.

tools.name: grafana_list_incidents
tools.description: List Grafana Incident records, filterable by status, severity, and label. Use to find ongoing or past incidents; returns IDs, titles, and timestamps. Paginated.

query.description: Text to match against incident titles.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response.

tasks.prompt: I don't remember the link, but there's a dashboard somewhere about Kafka consumer lag tagged 'streaming'. Can you track it down?
What panels and variables does the dashboard with uid 'abc123xy' have? I just want a quick overview, not the whole JSON.
Show me the 95th percentile of http_request_duration_seconds for the checkout service over the last 6 hours using the Prometheus datasource with uid prom-main.
Someone broke the 'API Latency' dashboard (uid api-lat-01) yesterday. Roll it back to version 14.
Pause the alert rule with uid 'hf92k1' while we do maintenance tonight.
Which Slack or email contact points do we have configured for alerts?

tools.name: splunk_run_search
tools.description: Runs a SPL search and waits for completion, returning results inline. Use for short, bounded queries that finish quickly. For long-running searches use splunk_create_search_job and poll instead. Results are capped by max_results; requires the search capability.

query.description: SPL query, e.g. 'index=main error | stats count by host'.

earliest_time.description: Start of time range, e.g. '-24h' or ISO 8601.

max_results.description: Maximum number of rows to return.

tools.name: splunk_create_search_job
tools.description: Creates an asynchronous search job and returns its search ID (sid) immediately. Use for long-running or large searches; then check progress with splunk_get_search_job and fetch output with splunk_get_search_results. For quick queries use splunk_run_search.

query.description: SPL query to execute.

timeout.description: Seconds to keep the job after it finishes.

tools.name: splunk_get_search_job
tools.description: Returns status of a search job by sid, including dispatch state, progress percentage, event count and scan count. Use to poll a job created with splunk_create_search_job. Does not return results.

tools.name: splunk_list_search_jobs
tools.description: Lists search jobs visible to the user with their sid, status, and query. Use to find a job you forgot the sid of. Supports pagination.

offset.description: Index of first job to return.

tools.name: splunk_get_search_results
tools.description: Fetches paginated results of a completed or in-progress search job. Use after splunk_create_search_job. Use splunk_get_search_events for raw events rather than transformed results.

tools.name: splunk_get_search_events
tools.description: Returns the raw events of a search job, not the transformed statistical results. Use when you need _raw and event metadata. Supports pagination.

tools.name: splunk_cancel_search_job
tools.description: Cancels and deletes a running or finished search job to free resources. Irreversible. Use for runaway searches.

tools.name: splunk_validate_search
tools.description: Parses an SPL query and reports syntax errors without running it. Use before executing complex queries. Returns parser messages and warnings.

query.description: SPL query to validate.

app.description: App context for macros and lookups.

tools.name: splunk_list_indexes
tools.description: Lists indexes available to the user with basic size and event count info. Use to discover where data lives; use splunk_get_index for full details of a single index.

tools.name: splunk_get_index
tools.description: Returns detailed configuration and statistics of a single index, including retention, max size, current size, min/max event time, and paths. Use after splunk_list_indexes.

tools.name: splunk_create_index
tools.description: Creates a new index. Requires admin privileges. Name must be lowercase and cannot start with underscore.

frozen_time_period_secs.description: Seconds before data is frozen or deleted.

tools.name: splunk_list_saved_searches
tools.description: Lists saved searches, reports and alerts. Use to find one by name or app; use splunk_get_saved_search for full definition. Paginated.

tools.name: splunk_get_saved_search
tools.description: Returns the full definition of a saved search: SPL, schedule, alert conditions, actions, and permissions.

tools.name: splunk_create_saved_search
tools.description: Creates a saved search, optionally scheduled or configured as an alert. Use splunk_update_saved_search to change an existing one.

tools.name: splunk_update_saved_search
tools.description: Modifies fields of an existing saved search such as query, schedule, or alert settings. Only provided fields change.

tools.name: splunk_delete_saved_search
tools.description: Permanently deletes a saved search or alert. Cannot be undone.

tools.name: splunk_run_saved_search
tools.description: Dispatches a saved search now and returns its sid. Use to execute an existing report rather than writing SPL.

tools.name: splunk_list_fired_alerts
tools.description: Lists recently fired alert instances, with trigger time and severity. Use to see what alerts triggered; use splunk_get_fired_alert for one alert group's details.

tools.name: splunk_get_fired_alert
tools.description: Returns triggered instances for a specific fired alert group, including sid and trigger time.

tools.name: splunk_list_dashboards
tools.description: Lists dashboards (views) with title, app and owner. Use splunk_get_dashboard to read a dashboard's XML.

tools.name: splunk_get_dashboard
tools.description: Returns the definition (Simple XML or Dashboard Studio JSON) of a dashboard along with its permissions.

tools.name: splunk_list_apps
tools.description: Lists installed Splunk apps with version and enabled state. Use to check whether an app is present.

tools.name: splunk_list_users
tools.description: Lists Splunk users with roles and email. Requires admin privileges (list_users capability).

tools.name: splunk_get_user
tools.description: Returns details for a single user including roles, default app, email, last login, and allowed indexes.

tools.name: splunk_list_roles
tools.description: Lists roles with capabilities and index access. Requires admin privileges.

tools.name: splunk_list_lookups
tools.description: Lists lookup table files and definitions. Use splunk_get_lookup_contents to read rows.

tools.name: splunk_get_lookup_contents
tools.description: Reads rows from a lookup table by running inputlookup. Limited by row count.

tools.name: splunk_send_event
tools.description: Sends a single event to an index through the HTTP Event Collector. Use for testing or ingesting small events; requires an HEC token.

tools.name: splunk_get_server_info
tools.description: Returns Splunk server information: version, build, OS, server name, license state, and mode. Use for health and compatibility checks.

tools.name: splunk_list_sourcetypes
tools.description: Lists sourcetypes known to the instance, with event counts when requested. Use to discover data formats before writing searches.

tasks.prompt: Run a quick query for the last 15 minutes in index=web that counts HTTP 500 errors by host, and show me the table.

What's the retention period and current size of the 'security_audit' index?
Which alerts fired in the last 24 hours?
Pull the raw log lines (not aggregated stats) from the finished search job with sid scheduler__admin__search__RMD5abc123.
